EV-BAT-001.headline: CATL CTP-3.0-A NMC 811 Module (Tesla Model 3) – Direct Second-Life Reuse Protocol
economic_assumptions: Direct reuse at $650 value avoids $120 repair and $60 testing costs, yielding a $530 net margin versus $450 refurbishment pathway.
Capex savings of $200 per module versus new NMC 811 pack procurement, achieving 100% ROI on the $60 testing investment within one deployment cycle.
Logistics and handling at ~$40 per 28 kg unit preserves 92% of the $650 reuse valuation, far exceeding the $140 recovery scrap floor.
Aggregating 100 modules generates $65,000 in second-life revenue versus $14,000 from recycling, a 4.6x value uplift per asset.
environmental_assumptions: Reusing the 28 kg NMC 811 module avoids ~1,200 kg CO2e of embodied emissions from virgin lithium, nickel, and cobalt extraction and cell manufacturing.
Conserves approximately 1.8 kg of lithium, 4.2 kg of nickel, and 0.9 kg of cobalt per module, reducing pressure on critical mineral supply chains.
Prevents 28 kg of aluminum and copper structural materials from entering scrap streams, saving ~450 kg CO2e in secondary smelting.
Extends functional life of 850-cycle cells to 1,500+ cycles in stationary storage, deferring end-of-life recycling by 3-5 years.

action_steps.title: De-energize & Verify
action_steps.description: Isolate CATL CTP-3.0-A module, verify 35 mΩ internal resistance, and confirm 87% SOH via BMS handshake before handling.

action_steps.title: Visual & Thermal Inspection
action_steps.description: Inspect NMC 811 cells for swelling, electrolyte leaks, and connector integrity on the 28 kg Tesla Model 3 module.

action_steps.title: Functional Validation Test
action_steps.description: Run 10-minute charge/discharge profile to validate 850-cycle history and confirm no hidden cell imbalance exceeding 50 mV.

action_steps.title: Re-certify & Re-pair
action_steps.description: Re-pair module with compatible BMS, update firmware, and certify 87% SOH for second-life energy storage deployment.

action_steps.title: Logistics & Deployment
action_steps.description: Log asset EV-BAT-001 into circular inventory, tag with QR, and dispatch to second-life storage integration partner.

EV-CEL-006.headline: Panasonic 2170-NCA Cell (EV-CEL-006) Precision Refurbishment Protocol
economic_assumptions: Refurbishing the 2020 Panasonic 2170-NCA cell at 76% SOH recovers ~65-70% of new-cell replacement cost, yielding a net margin of 35-45% after precision reconditioning and requalification testing.
Capex savings of approximately 40-50% versus procuring a new 5Ah NCA cell, with ROI on refurbishment equipment amortized over 18-24 months at current throughput.
Secondary-market resale value for a refurbished 76% SOH 2170-NCA cell supports a 25-35% premium over raw scrap recovery, maximizing revenue per cell.
Testing and logistics overhead is offset by the high residual value density of NCA chemistry, ensuring positive unit economics even at moderate refurbishment volumes.
environmental_assumptions: Refurbishment avoids ~8-12 kg CO2e of embodied emissions per cell by conserving the existing NCA cathode, copper current collectors, and aluminum casing versus virgin manufacturing.
Conserves approximately 0.5-0.8 g of lithium, 1.2-1.8 g of nickel, and 0.3-0.5 g of cobalt per cell, reducing pressure on primary extraction supply chains.
Preserves ~15-20 g of high-purity copper and ~8-12 g of aluminum in the cell envelope, avoiding energy-intensive smelting and refining cycles.
Extending service life by 2-3 years through refurbishment defers end-of-life recycling burden and reduces total lifecycle carbon intensity by an estimated 30-40%.

action_steps.title: Safe Discharge & Baseline Telemetry
action_steps.description: Discharge EV-CEL-006 to 2.5V via controlled current, verify 3.7V nominal and 5Ah capacity baseline, log internal resistance and thermal response.

action_steps.title: Physical & Electrochemical Inspection
action_steps.description: Inspect 2170-NCA casing for micro-fractures, seal integrity, and terminal corrosion; confirm no swelling or electrolyte leakage before proceeding.

action_steps.title: Precision Reconditioning Cycle
action_steps.description: Perform formation cycling at 0.5C to restore SEI stability, rebalance internal impedance, and recover SOH toward 80-82% target.

action_steps.title: Post-Refurb Qualification Testing
action_steps.description: Run full capacity, internal resistance, and thermal profiling tests; validate 3.7V/5Ah NCA spec compliance and 80%+ SOH threshold.

action_steps.title: Certification & Deployment
action_steps.description: Apply CogniCycle refurbishment certification label, log SOH and cycle data to digital passport, and stage for secondary-market deployment.

EV-ECU-017.headline: Continental ECU-PT-400 Direct Reuse Protocol
economic_assumptions: Direct reuse at $380 vs. $30 scrap recovery yields a $350 gross margin, a 12.7x value multiplier over recycling.
Avoided refurbishment Capex: skipping $60 repair and $35 testing saves $95 in processing costs, improving net margin to $325 after $20 logistics.
ROI on the $20 logistics spend is 1625%, making this the highest-leverage disposition in the ECU triage queue.
At 90% triage confidence, expected value of reuse ($342) exceeds refurbishment net ($125) by $217, confirming REUSE as the optimal pathway.
environmental_assumptions: Reuse avoids remanufacturing embodied CO2e of ~18 kg CO2e per ECU, conserving the full carbon footprint of the 2.5 kg unit.
Preserves embedded virgin materials: ~0.4 kg copper in PCB traces, ~0.1 kg aluminum heat-sink, and rare-earth elements in inductive components.
Extends functional life of the 2020 Continental ECU-PT-400 by an estimated 5-8 years, deferring new semiconductor fabrication and associated water/energy use.
Avoids e-waste landfill diversion for the 2.5 kg unit, including hazardous solder and electrolytic capacitors.

action_steps.title: Clear P0100 & Verify Telemetry
action_steps.description: Clear P0100 code via Continental diagnostic tool, verify no recurrence over 30-min drive cycle, log SOH and sensor outputs.

action_steps.title: Physical & Connector Inspection
action_steps.description: Inspect 2.5 kg ECU-PT-400 for connector wear, corrosion, and thermal discoloration; confirm no physical damage before release.

action_steps.title: Bench Functional Validation
action_steps.description: Run full functional bench test: CAN bus response, sensor input validation, and output actuation to confirm pass status.

action_steps.title: Tag, Certify & Log
action_steps.description: Apply CogniCycle REUSE label, record asset ID EV-ECU-017, and update inventory with 90% confidence disposition flag.

action_steps.title: ESD Packaging & Dispatch
action_steps.description: Package in anti-static ESD bag, ship to remanufacturing partner within 48h to minimize idle logistics cost.

CUSTOM-BAT-999.headline: VoltMax Na-Ion-1 Sodium Pack (Rivian R1T) — End-of-Life Recycling Protocol
economic_assumptions: Scrap recovery value for the 400 kg VoltMax Na-Ion-1 pack is estimated at $2,200, driven primarily by aluminum casing, copper busbars, and recoverable sodium compounds, yielding a net margin of ~$1,800 after $400 in disassembly and logistics costs.
Recycling avoids the $2,200 reuse valuation loss but captures 70-80% of embodied material value through hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical recovery of Al, Cu, and Na2SO4 precursors.
Capex savings of ~$1,500 per pack are realized by diverting from secondary-market refurbishment (which would require $800+ in cell balancing and BMS replacement) to direct material recovery.
ROI on the recycling line is positive at scale: processing 100 packs annually generates ~$180,000 in net material revenue against a $120,000 annualized facility cost, yielding a 1.5x return.
environmental_assumptions: Recycling the 400 kg VoltMax Na-Ion-1 pack avoids ~1,200 kg CO2e of embodied emissions by recovering aluminum (avoiding 11 t CO2e/t Al) and copper (avoiding 3.5 t CO2e/t Cu) from virgin smelting.

Sodium-ion chemistry eliminates critical mineral depletion: no lithium, nickel, or cobalt is lost, but ~180 kg of sodium sulfate and ~45 kg of iron are conserved for precursor reuse, reducing demand for mined Na2CO3.
Recovering ~120 kg of aluminum casing and ~35 kg of copper busbars per pack conserves virgin bauxite and copper ore, cutting upstream mining emissions by an estimated 450 kg CO2e per unit.

Proper pyrometallurgical processing of the Na-Ion-1 cells prevents release of residual electrolyte (NaPF6-based) and carbon anode particulates, avoiding ~200 kg CO2e of uncontrolled thermal decomposition emissions.

action_steps.title: De-energize & Verify Telemetry
action_steps.description: Verify 88% SOH and 120-cycle telemetry on VoltMax Na-Ion-1 BMS, confirm zero thermal events, and tag pack for recycling stream.

action_steps.title: Controlled Discharge & Lockout
action_steps.description: Discharge VoltMax Na-Ion-1 to 0 V via controlled load bank, confirm <1 V per cell, and apply lockout/tagout on 400 kg pack terminals.

action_steps.title: Pack Extraction & Module Separation
action_steps.description: Remove Rivian R1T mounting brackets, disconnect HV harness, and extract the 400 kg VoltMax Na-Ion-1 pack using certified EV lift equipment.

action_steps.title: Material Stream Segregation
action_steps.description: Separate aluminum casing, copper busbars, and Na-Ion-1 cell modules; route cells to pyrometallurgical line and metals to hydrometallurgical recovery.

action_steps.title: Recovery & Mass-Balance Audit
action_steps.description: Log recovered Al, Cu, Na2SO4, and Fe masses; generate mass-balance certificate and issue recycling compliance report for VoltMax Na-Ion-1.

EV-006.headline: Refurbishment Protocol: Samsung Display 12.3-OLED-EV Infotainment (VW ID.4)
economic_assumptions: Refurbishment yields a net margin of $564 ($764 refurb value - $92 repair - $70 testing - $39 logistics), representing a 75% return on $752 total investment.
Avoids $528 in value destruction versus full recycling ($764 refurb value vs. $84 recovery scrap value).
Repair cost of $92 is minimal relative to the $764 refurbishment value, indicating a low-cost intervention with high economic leverage.
Logistics cost of $39 represents only 5.2% of total refurbishment value, confirming efficient supply chain economics for this component.
environmental_assumptions: Refurbishment avoids embodied CO2e of approximately 45-60 kg CO2e associated with manufacturing a new 12.3-inch OLED display panel.
Conserves virgin materials including ~120g of indium (ITO), ~80g of rare-earth phosphors, and ~200g of copper in the display driver IC and FPCB.
Extends the functional life of the Samsung Display 12.3-OLED-EV by 3-5 years, deferring end-of-life e-waste and associated landfill emissions.
Reduces demand for new lithium and cobalt in the display's power management IC, conserving approximately 5-8g of Li and 2-3g of Co per unit.

action_steps.title: Safe Removal & ESD Prep
action_steps.description: Power down, disconnect 12V harness, and remove the 12.3-OLED-EV display assembly from the VW ID.4 dashboard using OEM fasteners.

action_steps.title: Diagnostic Isolation
action_steps.description: Bench-test the Samsung 12.3-OLED-EV panel to isolate the functional failure (e.g., driver IC, FPCB, or backlight circuit) using diagnostic software.

action_steps.title: Component-Level Repair
action_steps.description: Replace the failed component (driver IC or FPCB) with OEM-grade parts, reflow solder joints, and re-apply thermal interface material.

action_steps.title: Functional Validation
action_steps.description: Run full functional validation: pixel uniformity, touch response, brightness calibration, and thermal cycling per Samsung Display test spec.

action_steps.title: Reintegration & Documentation
action_steps.description: Reinstall the refurbished display into the VW ID.4, perform CAN bus integration test, and document SOH and serial number for traceability.

EV-020.headline: BorgWarner OBC-11kW (EV-020) Critical-Risk Recycling Protocol
economic_assumptions: Recovery scrap value of $73 (Cu, Al, NdFeB, SiC) minus $39 logistics and $59 testing yields a net negative margin of -$25, justifying expedited recycling over refurbishment ($479 value) given CRITICAL_RISK status.
Avoiding $108 repair cost and $107 combined testing/logistics on a degraded unit with no error codes but critical safety flags eliminates $215 in sunk Capex exposure.
Recycling bypasses the $761 reuse valuation entirely, but prevents potential $5,000+ liability from high-voltage thermal incidents on a 800V-rated unit.
Net economic outcome: -$25 direct cost offset by avoided liability and regulatory compliance, ROI neutral within 30-day processing window.
environmental_assumptions: Recycling 13.91 kg OBC-11kW recovers ~4.2 kg Cu, ~3.1 kg Al, and ~0.8 kg NdFeB magnets, avoiding 12.6 t CO2e embodied in virgin mineral extraction.
Conserving 0.8 kg NdFeB (Nd, Pr, Dy) avoids 28 t CO2e and 1.4 kg rare-earth ore processing per unit.
SiC power module recovery (~0.3 kg) prevents 9.2 t CO2e from virgin silicon carbide crystal growth.
Proper thermal management fluid and electrolyte capture avoids 0.4 t CO2e and prevents hazardous waste stream contamination.

action_steps.title: HV De-Energize & Lockout
action_steps.description: Isolate 800V DC bus, verify zero potential with CAT IV meter, apply lockout tags to BorgWarner OBC-11kW terminals.

action_steps.title: Disassemble & Segregate Materials
action_steps.description: Thermally stabilize unit, remove 13.91 kg assembly, segregate SiC power module and NdFeB motor drive section for material recovery.

action_steps.title: Material Stream Routing
action_steps.description: Route Cu windings, Al heat sinks, and NdFeB magnets to certified e-waste processor; document 73 USD recovery value.

action_steps.title: Safety Documentation & Ledger
action_steps.description: Log CRITICAL_RISK safety flags, degraded functional test, and 91.4% efficiency baseline to asset ledger for traceability.

action_steps.title: Final Verification & Closeout
action_steps.description: Confirm zero residual charge, certify thermal fluid capture, and close recycling ticket with 90% confidence disposition record.
